evidence_strength_mapping.rule: The graph schema enforces a strict 4-value evidence_strength enum {source_grounded, synthesis, inference, unconfirmed}; the Tier-3 records carry a richer descriptive string and a 5-value provenance vocabulary (incl. operator_confirmed). The authored node's canonical evidence_strength is derived by a pure, status-PRESERVING inverse of the record's declared validation_status, so the compiler's Appendix-B lookup reproduces the SAME §12.2 status the hand-lift declares:
evidence_strength_mapping.Assumed: unconfirmed      (Appendix-B -> Unresolved; + note; none present today)
evidence_strength_mapping.lossless: The original descriptive evidence_strength string is preserved verbatim in a pass-through 'provenance_detail' field so no provenance nuance is lost and the ticket-10 cutover has the full audit trail. Because the diff oracle converges by record identity (id/milestone_id), the canonical-enum representation converges cleanly; field-level reconciliation of the descriptive string is a ticket-10 concern.
evidence_strength_mapping.proposal_section_rule: Every proposal_section node is evidence_strength=synthesis (-> inferred). This is semantically correct and non-overclaiming: drafted evaluator narrative is SYNTHESIS OVER the confirmed Tier-3/2B substrate, never a raw source fact. It preserves each drafted section's real overall_status=inferred (the section JSONs carry only confirmed+inferred claims, no unresolved) and never dresses narrative as a source_grounded (Confirmed) fact — ticket-8 criterion 2. The section-level claims are C0n-tagged (not sub-section-attributed), so a per-sub-section confirmed/inferred split cannot be computed from the data; the section's claim distribution is carried on each node's provenance_detail for auditability.
